questions.q: Are there many museums in your hometown?
questions.answer: Not really. Sirajganj is a modest town, so there's nothing major. The best known is Tagore's old family estate at Shahzadpur, which has been turned into a museum and is quite [[atmospheric]].

Yes, actually. I find them fascinating, especially history museums, because they bring the past to life in a way books can't. I don't go nearly often enough, but each visit is genuinely [[enlightening]].

questions.q: When did you last visit a museum?
questions.answer: About a year ago, I went to the Liberation War Museum in Dhaka while visiting my sister. It was an incredibly moving experience, and some of the personal letters on display were genuinely [[harrowing]] to read.

questions.q: Did you go to museums on school trips?
questions.answer: Only once or twice, as school trips weren't very common where I grew up. I remember being [[captivated]] by the old coins and weapons, though, and asking the guide far too many questions.

questions.q: Do you think museums will still be popular in the future?
questions.answer: I think so, as long as they adapt. Young people expect interactive displays and digital content now, so museums that feel dull and [[static]] may struggle. But seeing real historical objects in person will always have its appeal.
